title: Intergroup Competition Promotes Intragroup Cooperation: A Meta-Analysis of Social Dilemmas
opposition_rationale: Competition and cooperation are an established bipolar pair formalised as a complement in social-dilemma payoff structures (defection vs cooperation), not lexical antonymy.
x_construct: intergroup competition (presence vs absence; manipulated) at the between-group level
opposite_construct: intragroup cooperation, i.e. reduced within-group defection, at the within-group level
study_design: preregistered multilevel random-effects meta-analysis of experimental game studies (25 articles, 70 effects, N=6051)
mediator: not isolated in accessible text; interdependence is the proximal condition
moderator: interdependence between groups (stronger effect with interdependence)
boundary_conditions: effect requires intergroup competition to be interdependent with intra-group payoffs; generalises across paradigms only within that regime
counterevidence: study motivated by mixed prior findings; no publication-bias or null result verifiable from the abstract
notes: Cross-level promotion claim, not a sign reversal of the same outcome; coded OCI under S4 because i and j differ on the level index. Body text not accessible (SAGE 403); coding rests on verified abstract + Crossref/OpenAlex/PubMed metadata.

title: Intergroup conflict: individual, group, and collective interests
opposition_rationale: Individual-, group- and collective-level rationality are formally incompatible in the payoff structures of mixed-motive/team games; admissible via domain theory specifying incompatible functional states.
x_construct: individually rational action (maximise own payoff) at the individual level
opposite_construct: collective irrationality: reduced group/collective payoff, i.e. the opposite of what the same rationality criterion prescribes at the collective level
study_design: theoretical essay plus narrative review of an authored laboratory programme; taxonomy of team games; no new data, no pooled estimate
mediator: payoff structure (which level of rationality is rendered binding)
moderator: game structure; theoretical vs behavioural conditions determining which level prevails
boundary_conditions: reversal holds only where payoffs make the levels strictly opposed; absent in purely cooperative or purely individual tasks
counterevidence: no disconfirming cases reported in the abstract; no quantitative test of when the reversal occurs
notes: Packet DOI 10.1207/S15327957PSPR0702_129-145 does not resolve; corrected identifier is 10.1207/s15327957pspr0702_129-145 (Bornstein 2003, PSPR 7(2), 129-145), hence source_verified=partial. Strongest formal fit in the conflict stratum.

title: Deterrence and International Conflict: Empirical Findings and Theoretical Debates
opposition_rationale: Deterrence theory and the spiral/security-dilemma model are a codified theoretical pair specifying incompatible predicted states of the same variable (threat posture vs probability of conflict).
x_construct: deterrent threat posture / military credibility at the state level
opposite_construct: conflict probability, whose direction the two theories predict oppositely
study_design: narrative state-of-the-field review of statistical tests and comparative case studies; no original data
mediator: adversary perception/response; credibility of threat
moderator: balance of forces, costly signalling, reputation, interests at stake
boundary_conditions: review's own framing is conditionality (when deterrence succeeds or fails), not an unconditional inversion
counterevidence: explicitly reports that empirical tests challenged theoretical arguments and sparked design debates
exclusion_reason: Record's own focal claim is conditionality of deterrence efficacy, not do(X)->O(X); the accumulation->insecurity reversal is not stated or tested in any text I could verify (Annual Reviews 403). Not credited from the concept name alone.
notes: Coded as a negative example to resist title-level cherry-picking. If the full text documents a spiral-model section, this record is likely to be a genuine A/B disagreement and should be adjudicated from the source, not from consensus.

title: Domestic Discontent and the External Use of Force
opposition_rationale: No admissible opposition: the paper contrasts two sources of domestic discontent, which is a construct refinement/moderator claim, not a bipolar pair or formal complement.
x_construct: presidential support erosion among coalition critics (time-series, US 1953-1976)
opposite_construct: none specified; outcome is external use of force short of war
study_design: observational time-series/event analysis with multiple empirical techniques; theory test of diversionary war
mediator: instrumental use of international conflict to repair domestic coalition support
moderator: origin of discontent (coalition-critical vs other groups)
boundary_conditions: conflicts short of war; US cases 1953-1976 only
counterevidence: reports the baseline null: quantitative tests generally failed to establish the systemic link
exclusion_reason: Moderated association between discontent and force use; no increasing-X-produces-its-opposite relation, and no causal identification beyond observational design.
notes: Packet stable_id JCR-1992-36-25 is not a registry identifier; matched real article is Morgan & Bickers 1992, JCR 36(1), 25-52, DOI 10.1177/0022002792036001002, hence source_verified=partial.

title: The Security Dilemma: A Conceptual Analysis
opposition_rationale: Security and insecurity are the same variable's incompatible states in security-dilemma theory (defensive provision generating counter-mobilisation); admissible via domain theory, and the paper is a definitional analysis of precisely that mechanism.
x_construct: unilateral security provision / armament by one actor at t0
opposite_construct: lowered security for the same actor after the adversary's reactive armament
study_design: conceptual/theoretical essay redefining the security-dilemma concept; no data, no formal estimates
mediator: adversary's threat perception of defensively intended actions
moderator: anarchy, ambiguity of intent, offensive-defensive asymmetry (conditions the paper critiques)
boundary_conditions: requires perceptual ambiguity of defensive intent; the author argues most extant extensions are inaccurate or misleading
counterevidence: author's own negative findings target concept-stretching rather than the reversal itself
notes: Packet journal is wrong: the article is Security Studies 18(3), 587-623 (ISSN 0963-6412), not Security Dialogue. Evidence tier E0 records absence of empirical identification, not scholarly quality; body text inaccessible (T&F 403), so the reversal is coded from the verified concept definition, which is the weakest inference in this packet and a likely A/B disagreement.

title: Can There Ever Be Too Many Options? A Meta-Analytic Review of Choice Overload
opposition_rationale: Assortment size and choice quality (deferral, dissatisfaction) are treated as functionally opposed states in the choice-overload literature; admissible via established construct pair, though the authors themselves attribute the 'paradox of choice' label to Schwartz.
x_construct: number of options available (large vs small assortment)
opposite_construct: effective choosing: deferral, lower choice probability, lower satisfaction
study_design: random-effects meta-analysis with meta-regression, trimming and funnel diagnostics (50 published and unpublished experiments, 63 conditions, N=5036)
mediator: decision difficulty and preference-representation strength (not estimated in this paper)
moderator: outcome type (consumption DV), expertise/clear prior preferences, publication status, year
boundary_conditions: authors state no sufficient conditions for overload could be identified
counterevidence: headline null (d=0.02, CI -0.09 to 0.12; trimmed d=0.001), slight publication bias, repeated replication failures, poor quadratic fit (R2=0.02)
notes: A null result is still an OCI candidate because the record tests the schema-shaped relation; the opposite-sign subgroup (people with clear preferences prefer larger sets) is the only positive reversal evidence here. Full text verified via the authors' open copy.

title: Choice overload: A conceptual review and meta-analysis
opposition_rationale: Same established construct pair as P06; the authors themselves describe the focal result as 'the paradoxical finding that providing individuals with more options can be detrimental to choice'.
x_construct: assortment size (number of options)
opposite_construct: choice quality: deferral, switching, dissatisfaction, regret
study_design: conceptual review plus meta-analysis (99 observations, N=7202) with moderator specification
mediator: processing burden implied by the four moderators; not separately estimated
moderator: choice set complexity, decision task difficulty, preference uncertainty, prominence of an effort-minimizing decision goal
boundary_conditions: reversal is moderator-gated; more options help when complexity, difficulty and uncertainty are low
counterevidence: conditional result contradicts prior meta-analytic data (P06's null); the corrigendum reports a null coefficient (b=.04, t(39)=.9) in the assortment-size table
notes: A corrigendum exists (10.1016/j.jcps.2015.07.001, JCP 26(2):312) correcting p.348; pooled magnitudes beyond the corrected coefficients are UNVERIFIED (paywalled).

title: The Autonomy Paradox: The Implications of Mobile Email Devices for Knowledge Professionals
opposition_rationale: Formal autonomy (choice over where/when to work) versus effective autonomy (actual control of work and time) is the schema's own construct-switch example, and the authors name the incompatible pair 'the autonomy paradox'.
x_construct: use of mobile email devices and the enacted norm of continual connectivity, framed by users as increasing individual autonomy
opposite_construct: reduced effective autonomy: working everywhere/all the time under escalated collective expectations
study_design: qualitative grounded-theory-style interview study (48 knowledge professionals, 2004-05; one firm plus snowball sample; 18 re-interviewed)
mediator: shift in collective expectations about 'what it takes' to be an effective professional
moderator: professional commitment to colleagues/clients, hierarchy and juniority
boundary_conditions: high-commitment professional settings with peer-judged availability; 2004-05 mobile email technology
counterevidence: participants largely did not report feeling trapped (they normalised the escalation); a few explicitly resisted; no detectable variation by gender, hierarchy or occupation
notes: Multi-index case: I code primary_mechanism=construct_substitution following the schema's example, while the authors' own causal story is a collective escalation, i.e. level_switch plus feedback; either assignment is defensible and this is the packet's clearest legitimate disagreement risk.

title: Self-Determination Theory Applied to Health Contexts: A Meta-Analysis
opposition_rationale: No bipolar or complementary pair is inverted: autonomy support and need satisfaction move in the same direction as self-determination; any opposite here would be lexical only.
x_construct: practitioner autonomy support
opposite_construct: none claimed
study_design: meta-analysis (184 independent data sets) with meta-analytic path analyses
mediator: need satisfaction and autonomous motivation (modelled as mediators of the same-direction chain)
moderator: age, study design (tested where effects were heterogeneous)
boundary_conditions: health contexts only
counterevidence: no reversal reported; the paper reports positive relations throughout
exclusion_reason: Monotonic-positive mediation; fails stage 1 requirement of an outcome opposite to the exposure and fails S4 because no index shift produces O(X).
notes: Retained as a negative control from the autonomy/choice stratum. Subscription-only text; coding from verified abstract.

title: Self-Determination Theory and Workplace Outcomes: A Meta-Analysis
opposition_rationale: Same as P09: the reported chain is same-direction, and the authors explicitly decline causal inference.
x_construct: perceived need support from workplace leaders
opposite_construct: none claimed
study_design: three-level meta-analysis plus meta-analytic structural equation modelling (192 articles, N=93552) with a full bias panel
mediator: need satisfaction; autonomous vs controlled motivation
moderator: work type, employee type, proximity of leader autonomy support, country GDP, cultural orientation
boundary_conditions: correlational data; authors call for randomised designs before causal claims
counterevidence: theory-predicted negatives not obtained (introjected and external regulation positively related to need support); hypotheses HM1a-c, HM2a-c, HM6, HM7 rejected
exclusion_reason: No functional-opposite outcome and no causal identification; rejected moderators are disconfirmation of predictions, not an inversion.
notes: Published not in press: Stress and Health 42(1), e70151, 10 Feb 2026, PMC12887546. Zero occurrences of paradox/backfire/boomerang in the full text.

title: Homo Heuristicus: Why Biased Minds Make Better Inferences
opposition_rationale: Information/computation and predictive accuracy are functionally opposed by the bias-variance account the authors formalise: beyond a point more input lowers the very quantity it is meant to raise. Not lexical antonymy.
x_construct: amount of information, cues, weights and computation used in inference
opposite_construct: predictive accuracy (the intended function of that information), decreased by overfitting
study_design: theory plus simulation and reanalysis of published datasets; no new human experiment
mediator: variance/overfitting: error decomposition bias^2 + variance + noise
moderator: linear predictability (R2 < .5), object-to-cue ratio <= 10, cue correlation, recognition validity > .5, training-sample size
boundary_conditions: authors state explicitly that less-is-more is a point beyond which more input is detrimental, not a monotone law
counterevidence: in the binary environment take-the-best performs worse than its greedy counterpart; the authors concede their bet can fail even at zero bias
notes: Nominal vs effective split is their own 'excel in hindsight, fail in foresight' formulation; publisher PDF verified.

title: Homo Ignorans: Deliberately Choosing Not to Know
opposition_rationale: Knowledge and ignorance are lexical antonyms, which the schema deems insufficient; what makes the pair admissible here is the cited functional evidence (feedback reducing performance, ignorance improving bargaining and impartiality), so validity is only partially established within the record.
x_construct: acquisition and use of information
opposite_construct: performance, bargaining payoff and agency, whose intended support information can invert
study_design: conceptual taxonomy; no new empirical test
mediator: emotion regulation, responsibility avoidance, impartiality, cognitive sustainability (six claimed functions)
moderator: whether action can follow the information; ambiguity plus egocentric bias; liability exposure; actor identity
boundary_conditions: 'efficient ignorance' only where expected damage to others is below the ignorer's gain
counterevidence: the paper itself flags harm from ignoring health information and concedes one pathway is 'purely speculative'
notes: No open-access copy of the journal article reached; quotations come from the authors' adapted Strungmann Forum chapter, which misstates its own issue number (issue 3, not 2).

title: Does ignorance love company? The social dynamics of information avoidance
opposition_rationale: Information availability and actual information acquisition are functionally opposed in the paper's own claim that sharing crowds out searching; admissible via the paper's formal volunteer's-dilemma framing rather than lexical antonymy.
x_construct: opportunity to share information with others (collective transparency)
opposite_construct: reduced private information seeking, i.e. less knowledge at the collective level
study_design: four behavioural studies (N=760) including a repeated interactive experiment where participants could inform others
mediator: social influence/mimicry of others' avoidance; volunteer's dilemma incentive to free-ride on others' searching
moderator: prevalence of the behaviour; preference type (selfish more influenced, prosocial consistent)
boundary_conditions: reversal requires that others can be informed; injunctive norms about avoidance flip with prevalence
counterevidence: mimicry produced no overall change in information avoidance or prosocial behaviour; only a minority acted as information spreaders
notes: Body text behind ScienceDirect/ZORA bot-blocks; coded from verified Crossref/OpenAlex record plus the publisher abstract and article highlights. Randomisation status of the key manipulation unverified, hence E3 not E4.

title: Implications of Rational Inattention
opposition_rationale: No opposite is defined: capacity is a budget allocated by optimisation, and the model's content is damping and delay, not an inverted function of attention.
x_construct: information-channel capacity (bits per unit time)
opposite_construct: none claimed
study_design: formal dynamic optimisation under a Shannon capacity constraint with LQ control and a permanent-income example
mediator: posterior uncertainty and signal-to-noise under a fixed capacity
moderator: capacity level, weight in the objective, marginal returns to capacity
boundary_conditions: requires bounded signal-to-noise; no general-equilibrium counterpart supplied
counterevidence: author describes the implications as 'mostly thinly supported speculation'; adjustment-cost models mimic the same smoothness
exclusion_reason: Rational inattention is an optimisation-under-constraint result; the paper makes no do(X)->O(X) claim and reports no empirical test. Its near-reversal (harder problems attract less capacity) is monotone in marginal returns.
notes: No abstract in Crossref/OpenAlex; verified against the author's manuscript whose 16-item reference list matches the published list exactly. Zero occurrences of paradox/perverse/backfire.

title: Social Value of Public Information
opposition_rationale: Public information precision and social welfare are linked through the paper's own welfare definition; the opposition is the schema's named outcome-inversion example, admissible as a formal complement in the outcome rather than lexical antonymy.
x_construct: precision/quantity of public information supplied to agents
opposite_construct: expected social welfare, i.e. the function public information is provided to serve
study_design: formal beauty-contest/island model with continuum of agents, quadratic loss, linear-normal solution plus appendix extensions
mediator: coordination motive causing agents to overweight the public signal relative to the social planner's weights
moderator: strategic complementarity weight r (needs r > 0.5), precision of private signals, correlated vs independent private noise
boundary_conditions: interior region only: reversal when beta > alpha/[(2r-1)(1-r)]; welfare monotone positive absent socially valuable private information; corner alpha=0 under costly precision
counterevidence: always-beneficial case with no private information; strategic substitutes reverse the bias direction; adjacent Cao-Hirshleifer result differs in mechanism
notes: Cleanest formal OCI in the packet, with its own boundary conditions stated. Published AER 92(5), 1521-1534; the article's page header dates the issue December 2002 while Crossref prints 2002-11-01. Authors use 'detrimental', 'crowd out', 'more harm than good', not 'paradox'.

title: The Constructive, Destructive, and Reconstructive Power of Social Norms
opposition_rationale: A conservation-promoting message producing higher consumption in low-use households is a function-inversion of the message's defined purpose; admissible via the paper's theoretical prediction, not lexical antonymy.
x_construct: descriptive norm feedback about peers' consumption (intended to reduce use)
opposite_construct: increased household consumption, i.e. the opposite of the message's function
study_design: randomised field experiment with meter readings across three waves (approx. 300 households, San Marcos CA)
mediator: perceived descriptive norm inferred from the message
moderator: baseline consumption relative to the neighbourhood average; presence of an injunctive approval/disapproval signal
boundary_conditions: reversal occurs only below the reference average; the injunctive-smiley framing eliminates it
counterevidence: independent field evidence contradicts the boomerang in the lowest decile (Allcott & Rogers, NBER w15386, +3.4%); the negative-feedback face added nothing over information alone
notes: Quantitative magnitudes UNVERIFIED (publisher and repository PDFs blocked; figures seen only via the author's conference slides). Section 6 has no social-comparison family; level_switch chosen (individual behaviour vs group reference frame), with construct_switch also yes.

title: Do descriptive norms messaging interventions backfire? Protocol for a systematic review of the boomerang effect
opposition_rationale: The boomerang is defined as desirable behaviour becoming less likely after exposure to descriptive information, i.e. an inversion of the message's function; the protocol states this definition explicitly.
x_construct: descriptive-norms message content among people already behaving well
opposite_construct: decreased frequency of that behaviour
study_design: PRISMA-P systematic-review protocol (PROSPERO CRD42020156989); no screening results, no estimates
mediator: none estimated; planned moderator analysis of pre-intervention behaviour subgroup
moderator: pre-intervention behaviour level, message framing, delivery modality
boundary_conditions: English-only, restricted databases, studies without pre-intervention measures excluded
counterevidence: protocol states existing boomerang studies yielded inconsistent results, citing a null among lighter-than-average drinkers
notes: Candidate status rests on S4 (the target claim is representable); its contribution to the evidence base is nil, which is what E0 and result_support=not_tested record. Backfire/boomerang are the authors' own operative terms.

title: Iatrogenic effects of psychosocial interventions for substance use disorders: prevalence, predictors, prevention
opposition_rationale: Deterioration is the functional opposite of the intervention's definitionally specified purpose, and the paper quantifies it, so the opposition is admissible on domain-theoretic grounds rather than by antonymy.
x_construct: participation in psychosocial treatment or prevention (exposure to group-based intervention)
opposite_construct: post-treatment functioning below pre-treatment functioning
study_design: narrative critical review of controlled trials of treatment and prevention plus a conceptual framework
mediator: deviancy modelling and peer contagion within group delivery; confrontation, criticism and high emotional arousal
moderator: younger age, unmarried status, more severe diagnoses and use problems, more psychiatric and interpersonal problems; weak bonding and low monitoring
boundary_conditions: a significant minority, not the average participant: 7-15% worse off after treatment; prevention programmes raised expectations and use
counterevidence: author states research is still needed to determine whether deterioration is iatrogenic; predictors labelled probable
notes: Harm is attributed to group-level composition acting on individuals, hence level_switch as primary with actor_switch flagged. Body text beyond the structured abstract UNVERIFIED (Wiley 403).

title: Psychological Treatments That Cause Harm
opposition_rationale: Objective deterioration co-occurring with reported benefit, plus paradoxical anxiety increase during an anxiety-reduction procedure, are function-inversions specified by clinical theory rather than lexical opposites.
x_construct: dose of a specified psychological treatment or prevention programme
opposite_construct: enduring client deterioration relative to no treatment, and symptom worsening in the targeted domain
study_design: narrative critical review plus conceptual taxonomy; aggregates others' RCTs and meta-analyses with reported effect sizes
mediator: premature termination of exposure to anxiety-provoking stimuli; vicarious modelling of maladaptive coping
moderator: diagnosis and subgroup (normal vs traumatic grief, panic-prone patients, early adolescence)
boundary_conditions: the author's definition requires enduring harm, excluding short-term exacerbation, and demands Level I or II evidence
counterevidence: boot-camp meta-analysis found no significant overall effects and no moderators explaining the split (9 positive, 8 iatrogenic, 12 null); peer-programme and DARE support is weak; CISD harm post-hoc at one time point
notes: PMID 26151919 is high only because of retrospective deposit; the record is Lilienfeld 2007, Perspectives on Psychological Science 2(1), 53-70, DOI 10.1111/j.1745-6916.2007.00029.x. Nominal-vs-effective split (recipients report benefit while objective indices worsen) drives the mechanism choice.

title: Effects of normative feedback for drinkers who consume less than the norm: Dodging the boomerang
opposition_rationale: Same norm-referenced function inversion as P16, defined against a threshold at the local norm; the authors state the predicted increase explicitly.
x_construct: personalised descriptive-norm feedback delivered to drinkers below the local norm
opposite_construct: increased drinks per week, the opposite of the intervention's function
study_design: secondary reanalysis of four parallel randomised controlled trials with assessment-only controls; mixed-effects ANOVA per sample
mediator: awareness of discrepancy from the norm (the assumed boomerang route, untested here)
moderator: intervention composition and delivery modality (computer only vs counsellor-delivered multi-component), baseline position relative to the local norm, follow-up timing
boundary_conditions: norm position defined relative to the local campus norm, not an absolute light-drinking definition
counterevidence: no boomerang emerged in any of the four samples (all interactions ns, one in the reduction direction); the paper concedes its subsamples are underpowered and that campaign colleges did show increases (Wechsler et al. 2003)
notes: An unobserved reversal in a test of the exact schema relation: kept as a candidate with result_support=no per the handoff's explicit instruction. Author manuscript at PMC4169697 read in full.

title: Jevons’ Paradox revisited: The evidence for backfire from improved energy efficiency
opposition_rationale: Efficiency improvement and cumulative resource use are functionally opposed in the paradox's own definition, with a 100%-rebound threshold operationalising the opposition; admissible via domain theory and an outcome complement, not lexical antonymy.
x_construct: economically justified energy-efficiency improvement at the device or partial-equilibrium level
opposite_construct: economy-wide energy use, increased rather than reduced
study_design: critical conceptual and empirical review of the Jevons/Brookes/Saunders case; no original econometric estimate
mediator: rebound: productivity, price and income effects feeding aggregate demand and growth
moderator: rebound magnitude relative to the 100% backfire threshold; role of energy in driving productivity and growth
boundary_conditions: backfire requires rebound > 100%; the inference from partial to economy-wide equilibrium is where the case weakens
counterevidence: the paper's own conclusion is that evidence for Jevons' Paradox is far from conclusive, with empirical and theoretical weaknesses identified in the strong claim
notes: Abstract-level verification only (Elsevier and figshare copy 403); no rebound figure could be confirmed, so no numeric claim is coded. Authors use 'Paradox' and 'backfire'.

title: The road to hell is paved with good intentions: A review and research agenda on rebound effects and win–win strategies
opposition_rationale: The paper's contribution is a formal construct distinction: technical eco-efficiency gains versus realised ends, named means-ends decoupling, which specifies incompatible functional states.
x_construct: efficiency improvements and win-win strategies adopted to raise environmental performance
opposite_construct: realised environmental performance, partially or fully offset by increased demand
study_design: systematic literature review with bibliometrics and content analysis, plus a conceptual taxonomy and research agenda (156 references)
mediator: rebound as means-ends decoupling: how decision-makers perceive, manage or ignore rebound
moderator: type of win-win strategy and whether rebound is understood and acted upon
boundary_conditions: authors target clarification of when win-win claims are unreliable; the four types' boundary conditions are unstated at the accessible level
counterevidence: states the field has not systematically engaged with rebound; no quantitative synthesis or null result reported
notes: OnlineFirst status confirmed: published 6 May 2026, no volume/issue/pagination yet, 0 citers. Title proverb is rhetorical but the operative terms are technical; body text 403 from Wiley, so taxonomy detail is UNVERIFIED.

title: Braess' paradox: Some new insights
opposition_rationale: Travel cost and network capacity are formal complements in the equilibrium definition; the paradox is a proven existence result with stated parameter conditions, not antonymy.
x_construct: addition of a link (capacity augmentation) in a congested network
opposite_construct: higher total system travel cost at decentralised user equilibrium
study_design: formal analytical study of the classical Braess configuration with user-equilibrium assignment and congestion functions; no field data
mediator: route-choice externality: each user's response to the new link raises others' costs
moderator: congestion-function parameters, network topology, total demand level, presence of marginal-cost pricing
boundary_conditions: occurs only for total demand in an intermediate range whose bounds depend on congestion parameters; marginal-cost pricing restores the intended gain over stated ranges
counterevidence: the paper's own second result is a deflation: adding a link need not raise costs under pricing, and the paradox is not generic
notes: RePEc abstract verified; journal confirmed as Transportation Research Part B 31(3), 265-276. Numeric bounds UNVERIFIED (closed text).

title: Bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review of the traffic paradoxes (1968–2022)
opposition_rationale: The review restates the formal complement at issue (link addition raising cost for all users); the opposition is inherited from the underlying models rather than lexically asserted.
x_construct: network, capacity or information changes (link addition, mode substitution, information provision)
opposite_construct: higher travel cost for all users, and analogous cost increases in the dynamic and multimodal variants
study_design: bibliometric analysis plus systematic literature review of the traffic-paradox literature 1968-2022; no original test or estimate
mediator: assignment regime (user vs system optimum) as the review's organising mechanism
moderator: network topology, demand level, static vs dynamic assignment, mode substitution, information provision
boundary_conditions: the review's own scope condition: paradoxes are classified as static, dynamic, multimodal, other, and applied observations
counterevidence: no claim that the paradoxes fail in real networks could be verified from the accessible abstract
notes: Classification-only contribution; candidate status comes from the representability of the anchor claim it synthesises, so E2/weak/not_tested carry the evidence discount. Corpus sizes and per-theme counts UNVERIFIED (text closed). Primary mechanism assigned to the anchor Braess case; the informational and multimodal variants differ.

title: Safe development paradox: evidence and methodological insights from a systematic review
opposition_rationale: Realised safety and realised risk are the same indexed variable's opposed states, with the paper's own mechanism (protected development plus false sense of safety) specifying the incompatibility; a named sub-phenomenon (levee effect) operationalises it.
x_construct: investment in hazard risk-reduction measures (levees and dams, insurance, land-use rules, codes)
opposite_construct: long-run realised flood risk and damage, increased
study_design: ROSES-standard systematic review of empirical case studies (158 records screened to 40 analysed), no pooled effect estimate
mediator: development inside protected areas; reduced preparedness/false sense of safety; amplified damage from rare events
moderator: policy spatial scale (district and municipal plans more prone than regional or state); non-structural measures can both enhance and mitigate
boundary_conditions: requires residual risk: events exceeding the protection structure; long-run horizon
counterevidence: 1 of 40 studies refutes the pattern, 2 inconclusive; 40% are exposure-only with overestimation risk; heterogeneity prevented meta-analysis; the methods rule coding studies with ongoing mitigation as confirming is itself an inflation risk
notes: Open access, full text read. Time reversal chosen as primary because the paper's claim is short-run safety versus long-run damage; actor_switch (state builds, households develop) and construct_switch (protected is not flood-free) are also satisfied.

title: Toward a Theory of Paradox: A Dynamic Equilibrium Model of Organizing
opposition_rationale: The unit of analysis is a persistent tension pair whose poles coexist; no variable's functional opposite is produced by increasing it, and the model's claim is oscillation toward dynamic equilibrium.
x_construct: competing demand poles (e.g. exploration vs exploitation) managed over time
opposite_construct: none: both poles coexist rather than one being the inverted state of the other
study_design: theoretical essay and conceptual review proposing a dynamic-equilibrium model; no new data
mediator: cyclical responses to paradoxical tensions
moderator: environmental dynamism and competitiveness intensifying tensions
boundary_conditions: applies to persistent, interdependent polarities, not to reversible states
counterevidence: notes fundamental debates in the literature it reviews
exclusion_reason: Organising-tension theory: no do(X_i up) -> O(X)_j up representation. Over-emphasis produces a reactive shift to the other pole, which is oscillation, not the production of an opposite by its own increase.
notes: High-value negative example: the most-cited general 'theory of paradox' fails the strict definition, which is exactly what the schema's S5 and S7 exclusions anticipate. Body text 403 (AOM); the widely attributed typology is deliberately not used.

title: Dynamic Decision Making: A Model of Senior Leaders Managing Strategic Paradoxes
opposition_rationale: No admissible opposition is defined in the accessible text; the claims concern inconsistent handling of interwoven tensions, not one construct producing its inverse.
x_construct: senior-leader decision and framing practices vis-a-vis strategic tensions
opposite_construct: none specified
study_design: qualitative process study informing a model; abstract verifies six leadership teams, further design detail unobtainable
mediator: differentiating and integrating framing practices; temporal sequencing of decisions
moderator: none quantified
boundary_conditions: six teams in large firms; generalisation explicitly limited
counterevidence: whether any team's paradox framing failed could not be verified
exclusion_reason: Process model of tension management; no indexed causal inversion claim and no identification. Retained as a negative example.
notes: The phrase 'consistent inconsistency' appeared only in a retrieval summary of the abstract and could not be verified verbatim, so it is not used in coding. AOM full text 403; no OA copy located.

title: Over-optimization of academic publishing metrics: observing Goodhart's Law in action
opposition_rationale: A measure's informational validity and its optimisation are specified as incompatible states by Goodhart's Law, which the paper names and demonstrates; admissible via domain theory and outcome complement.
x_construct: degree to which a bibliometric measure is used as an evaluation target (and optimised)
opposite_construct: the measure's validity, informativeness and accuracy, which are destroyed
study_design: large-scale descriptive bibliometric trend analysis (>120M papers, 528M references, >20k journals, >2600 fields) with no inferential statistics
mediator: inflation channels: more authors, shorter papers, longer reference lists, self-citation, volume surge, 'academic clickbait', editor risk-aversion
moderator: extent to which a field or journal treats the measure as a target; hypercompetitive evaluation environment
boundary_conditions: the claim is historical and descriptive: measures degrade as they become targets; no counterfactual identification offered
counterevidence: authors allow other factors, offer hypercompetition as an alternative account, contradict Fanelli & Lariviere on productivity, and flag the post-2014 paper-count decline as a data artifact
notes: Open access full text read (PMC6541803). Nominal count keeps rising while the function collapses, so construct_switch is the primary index; no 'paradox' or 'backfire' in the authors' own prose, only Goodhart's and Campbell's Law.

title: Core capabilities and core rigidities: A paradox in managing new product development
opposition_rationale: Capabilities and their 'dysfunctional flip side' (core rigidities) are a named, theoretically specified incompatible pair with their own generative mechanisms, satisfying the domain-theory route.
x_construct: depth and entrenchment of a firm's core capabilities (technical systems, managerial systems, skills, values)
opposite_construct: inflexibility that blocks the same firm's new product and process development
study_design: theoretical essay illustrated by 20 case studies across five firms; no statistical test
mediator: values as the fourth dimension rooting the other three; protective routines and inherited problem-solving
moderator: environmental/technological discontinuity, which flips an operating-level asset into an innovation-level liability
boundary_conditions: reversal is regime-conditional: capabilities enable routine performance but inhibit development under discontinuity
counterevidence: no disconfirming case identifiable from the accessible abstract
notes: The abstract itself frames it as a paradox ('how to take advantage of capabilities without being hampered by their dysfunctional flip side'). The three standard rigidity mechanisms could not be verified from accessible text and are excluded. OpenAlex carries an abridged version of one abstract clause; AOM/Wiley full text 403.

title: Counterfinality: On the Increased Perceived Instrumentality of Means to a Goal
opposition_rationale: Detrimentality to an alternative goal and instrumentality for the focal goal are specified as inversely related by the authors' own contrast with the dilution effect; admissible via domain theory and an outcome complement rather than lexical antonymy.
x_construct: perceived detrimentality/cost of a means to an alternative goal
opposite_construct: perceived instrumentality/effectiveness of that same means for the focal goal
study_design: five experiments (one correlational survey, three randomised between-subjects experiments, one moderated-mediation study; total N approximately 692 plus 48 raters)
mediator: perceived detrimentality (pain, burning sensation) feeding inferred instrumentality
moderator: focal-goal magnitude x alternative-goal magnitude x detrimentality (three-way, replicated: b=0.22, p=0.009 and b=0.22, p=0.002, dR2=0.04)
boundary_conditions: reversal appears only when commitment to both the focal and the alternative goal is high; the outcome is perceived, not actual, instrumentality
counterevidence: all main effects and two-way interactions were null or marginal in Studies 4 and 5; the authors concede possible underpowered studies, a mixed two-sided-communication literature, and a momentary rather than durable picture
notes: Two internal reporting inconsistencies noted (a p=0.779 with b=-0.28; a b=0.55 with CI [0.87,1.01] excluding it), so effect claims are read conservatively. Reversal is epistemic (judgement), which is why construct_switch is the primary index. Full text read (Frontiers XML).
